stem: By what percent did the estimated number of adult wood frogs at the pond decrease from 2021 to 2023?
stimulus:
Each spring, volunteers estimate the number of adult wood frogs that come back to a pond to breed. Their estimates for three years are shown.

Estimated Adult Wood Frogs at the Pond
Year | 2019 | 2021 | 2023
Frogs | 320 | 400 | 300
explanation: The original value is the 2021 estimate, 400, and the new value is the 2023 estimate, 300. Percent change $= \frac{300 - 400}{400} \times 100 = -25\%$. The population went down by $25\%$.

B.why: You divided the drop of 100 by the 2023 value, 300, but the denominator has to be the original value. Here that is the 2021 estimate, 400.

C.why: You worked out $\frac{300}{400} = 75\%$. That tells you the 2023 population is 75% OF the 2021 population. It is not the percent decrease, which is $100\% - 75\% = 25\%$.

D.why: You stopped at the raw drop of 100 frogs and called it a percent. To get a percent, you still have to divide that difference by the original value, 400.

stem: The mean spring discharge is what percent of the mean late-summer discharge?
stimulus: A hydrologist recorded the discharge of a mountain river at one gauging station. During spring snowmelt, the mean discharge was 1,250 cubic meters per second. In late summer, the mean discharge was 500 cubic meters per second.
explanation: The question asks what percent the spring value is OF the late-summer value, so the late-summer discharge is the base and you do not subtract anything. $\frac{1{,}250}{500} \times 100 = 250\%$.

A.why: You worked out $\frac{500}{1{,}250} = 40\%$, which is the late-summer discharge as a percent of the spring discharge. The question asks for the reverse.

B.why: You subtracted to get 750 and then divided by the spring value, 1,250. That uses the wrong base, and the question also never asked for a change.

C.why: $150\%$ is how much greater the spring discharge is than the late-summer discharge. The question asks what percent the spring value is OF the late-summer value, which is $100\% + 150\% = 250\%$.

stem: By what percent did the average daily number of vehicles crossing the bridge increase from 2018 to 2024?
stimulus:
A city widened a two-lane bridge in 2021. Traffic engineers counted vehicles on the bridge before and after the work. The table shows the average daily number of vehicles crossing the bridge in three years.

Average Daily Vehicle Crossings
Year | 2018 | 2021 | 2024
Vehicles | 16,000 | 20,000 | 18,000
explanation: Compare the two years the question names. The 2021 value only sits in between. $\frac{18{,}000 - 16{,}000}{16{,}000} \times 100 = \frac{2{,}000}{16{,}000} \times 100 = 12.5\%$.

A.why: You compared 2021 with 2024 and found a 10% decrease from 20,000 to 18,000. The question asks about the change from 2018 to 2024.

C.why: You found the two separate changes, +25% and −10%, and added them. Successive percent changes multiply: $1.25 \times 0.9 = 1.125$, which is a 12.5% increase.

D.why: You worked out $\frac{18{,}000}{16{,}000} = 112.5\%$. That tells you the 2024 count is 112.5% OF the 2018 count. The increase is only $12.5\%$.

stem: By what percent did the drying time increase when the printmaker switched from the old ink to the new ink?
stimulus: A printmaker makes linocut prints with an oil-based ink. With the old ink, a finished print needed 36 hours to dry before it could be stacked. The printmaker then switched to a new ink with a richer pigment, and the drying time became 2.25 days.
explanation: First put both times in the same unit: 2.25 days is $2.25 \times 24 = 54$ hours. The original time is 36 hours, so percent change $= \frac{54 - 36}{36} \times 100 = \frac{18}{36} \times 100 = 50\%$.

A.why: You stopped at the raw difference of 18 hours and called it a percent. You still have to divide that 18 by the original 36 hours.

B.why: You divided the 18-hour increase by the new time, 54 hours. The denominator has to be the original drying time, 36 hours.

D.why: You worked out $\frac{54}{36} = 150\%$. That tells you the new drying time is 150% OF the old one. The increase is $150\% - 100\% = 50\%$.

stem: By what percent did the number of hand looms in the town decrease from 1810 to 1830?
stimulus: A historian used tax records to count the working hand looms in a weaving town every ten years as power looms spread through the region. The results are shown in the graph.

figure.caption: Working Hand Looms in the Town, 1800–1840
figure.alt: Line graph of working hand looms by decade: 300 in 1800, 360 in 1810, 330 in 1820, 240 in 1830, and 150 in 1840.

explanation: From the graph, there were 360 looms in 1810 and 240 in 1830. Percent change $= \frac{240 - 360}{360} \times 100 = -\frac{120}{360} \times 100 = -33\frac{1}{3}\%$. The number of looms went down by $33\frac{1}{3}\%$.

A.why: You used the 1800 value, 300, as the starting point and got $\frac{60}{300} = 20\%$. The question starts in 1810, when there were 360 looms.

C.why: You divided the drop of 120 by the 1830 value, 240. The denominator has to be the original value, the 1810 count of 360.

D.why: You worked out $\frac{240}{360} = 66\frac{2}{3}\%$. That tells you the 1830 count is that percent OF the 1810 count. The decrease is the rest: $33\frac{1}{3}\%$.
